lines.t: If the sound cuts out…
Does the love still speak?
Walk it.
Yeah.
Walk it.
Walk it, walk it—
Put some feet on that faith.
Talk is easy—
Love’s a choice you gotta make.
Hands up, then hands out,
Let the mercy leave the place.
When the whole crowd goes home,
Does your life still give Him praise?
Walk it, walk it—
Less about my name.
Walk it, walk it—
Love without a stage.
Had a clean white shirt with a grudge underneath,
Said “peace” out loud, kept war in my teeth.
Had a highlight reel of the good I’d done,
Cropped out the days I was helping no one.
Wanted front-row light, not the back-room broom,
Wanted God in my plans, not to give Him room.
Then I read those words, had to sit with that—
Was I chasing His will or a room that clapped?
Now the phone goes down when a friend needs time,
No lens on the meal that I leave outside.
Got a name in my head I’ve been scared to call,
Gotta say “I was wrong,” no excuse at all.
That’s a hard first step, but I’m taking it,
Can’t pray for a change and keep faking it.
Lord, get to the root, not the leaves I show—
If I’m holding on to pride, help me let that go.
You see the heart behind the sound,
The person when nobody’s ’round.
Let what I do when no one sees
Be true to what I say I believe.
Walk it, walk it—
Put some feet on that faith.
Talk is easy—
Love’s a choice you gotta make.
Hands up, then hands out,
Let the mercy leave the place.
When the whole crowd goes home,
Does your life still give Him praise?
Walk it, walk it—
Less about my name.
Walk it, walk it—
Love without a stage.
I was fluent in the words, slow with the welcome,
Quick to see a wound, slow to try to help one.
Told myself, “Somebody else can meet that need,”
While I asked You for a purpose You had put in front of me.
Now there’s room at the table, pull another chair,
Let the lonely take their time, I ain’t going anywhere.
And the one I disagree with still deserves my care—
Can’t claim I love my neighbor if there’s always fine print there.
I don’t get to choose who is worth my patience,
Or turn somebody’s worst day into conversation.
Keep my mouth from the spark that can burn their name,
Let me cover them with kindness, not collect their shame.
And if correction hits, let me hear it through,
Not defend an old habit ’cause it’s comfortable.
YahuShua, lead—let my own will yield;
Make the love I rap about something people feel.
When nobody knows?
(Still show love!)
When it costs you time?
(Still show love!)
When they don’t clap back?
(Still show love!)
Not to earn Your mercy—
But because I’ve known Your love.
I can’t buy what You have given,
Can’t perform my way to peace.
So I bring the heart I’ve hidden,
Let Your truth uncover me.
Not a louder reputation,
Not another polished line—
Let surrender be the rhythm
Of this ordinary life.
Walk it, walk it—
Put some feet on that faith.
Talk is easy—
Love’s a choice you gotta make.
Hands up, then hands out,
Let the mercy leave the place.
When the whole crowd goes home,
Does your life still give Him praise?
Walk it, walk it—
Less about my name.
Walk it, walk it—
Love without a stage.
If the sound cuts out…
Does the love still speak?
